punchline: Lottery winners were not much happier than controls, and accident victims were less unhappy than expected.
thirty_sec: In 1978 Brickman, Coates and Janoff-Bulman compared Illinois lottery winners, people paralysed in accidents and a control group. Winners rated themselves about as happy as the controls and victims only moderately lower, a sign of adaptation; later work added caveats.
question: Which change you are hoping for would still feel exciting on an ordinary Tuesday a year after you got it?
key_contrast: People adapt more than they predict, so pick goals for the ordinary days.
